resources.string: Hide the … button. The phone’s Back button or back gesture opens the emulator menu instead of sending Back to Android. Guest navigation buttons still control Android.
Forward legacy guest vibration to the phone. Applies on next boot; each pulse is capped at 60 seconds.
Swipe the circle above the navigation bar to roll; tap to select.
Off: real relative trackball events for guest apps. On: D-pad key presses instead. Does not send both.
Sensitivity: %1$d dp per step (lower is faster)

Let the guest scan, pair-list, and talk to Bluetooth devices through the phone: classic serial (RFCOMM) and Bluetooth LE (GATT). Needs Bluetooth permission and a full VM restart. Not raw HCI: the guest sees the phone adapter through a bridge, so headsets (audio profiles) are not supported.

If SurfaceFlinger crashes, let the firmware write a normal tombstone to the log (with the crashing function) instead of a short report. Use it when sending a bug report. Applies at the next full VM boot.
Bluetooth permission denied: the guest will boot without host Bluetooth.

Registers a touchpad and a keyboard in the guest and removes its touch screen. The screen becomes a touchpad (tap to click, two fingers to scroll) and a keyboard button appears in the navigation bar. Needs the QEMU engine (not the native 64-bit one) and a full VM restart.
Adds a keypad button to the navigation bar: arrow keys, OK, soft keys, Call/End and 0–9 * # like a feature phone. Touch keeps working and it can be combined with mouse and keyboard.
Drag a corner of the screen to resize it. Open the menu and tap Done resizing when finished.
